target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Barneby's revision documents representative Dalea hallii records from Hays, Kerr, and Kendall counties along the Balcones Escarpment and Edwards Plateau margin. Current Kew accepts D. hallii as an east-central Texas endemic.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the leaves and flower spikes. Hall's prairie clover is a slender perennial with mostly 3-foliolate leaves, sparse wiry stems, and relatively loose spikes of conspicuous yellow flowers. The calyx ribs/teeth are often reddish-brown and hairy.
diagnostic_traits: calyx ribs and teeth often red/chestnut-brown
calcareous prairie and rocky limestone habitat

comparisons.key_distinctions: Unlike purple-flowered D. purpurea, D. hallii has yellow flowers and typically 3-foliolate leaves. Unlike D. candida, the spikes are looser and flowers yellow rather than white.
